note: Resolves differences found by dual-stack-sweep.py. category_defaults override the script's built-in defaults (TEXT_ONLY/JAVA_UNHANDLED_500/JAVA_RAW_HTTP_4XX accepted; RUST_FAILS_WHERE_JAVA_OK/RUST_OTHER_CODE fail the run; the rest are OPEN backlog; any non-TEXT_ONLY difference inside a scripted journey fails unless an override says otherwise). An override must name the endpoint, may narrow by variant/category, and must say why the difference is acceptable or still open.

overrides.note: Embedded-JSON identity comparison limitation, not a paper/projection difference: five snapshot list strings contain independently generated question UUIDs that sweep cannot normalize inside strings. The isolated self-test probe JSON-parses each list and recursively normalizes generated identities; all fields/values match, including hidden answer placeholders, omitted analysis and completion blank slots. No data path is masked.

Same embedded-JSON generated-question-identity limitation as detail-active. The isolated probe parses all five projected lists and verifies exact normalized question content; exam and candidate fields compare normally. No data path is masked.

Candidate content is a JSON string containing independently generated question UUIDs. Sweep normalizes standalone UUIDs, not UUIDs embedded in strings. The isolated probe parses content recursively and verifies all answers/flags/fields match. No data path is masked.

The returned candidate content embeds the independently generated single-choice question UUID. Parsed and recursively normalized content is identical in the isolated probe; state 1 and saved answer are preserved on both stacks. No data path is masked.

Projected snapshot lists and preserved candidate content are JSON strings with independently generated question UUIDs. The isolated probe parses them, proves identical normalized content and asserts reentry preserves the previously saved A answer instead of overwriting it. No data path is masked.

Answer content embeds the independently generated question UUID. The isolated probe parses and recursively normalizes it and verifies identical stored content; the full candidate entity shape now matches Java. No data path is masked.

Reviewed snapshot lists and scored answer content embed independently generated question UUIDs in JSON strings. The isolated probe parses both recursively, verifies identical normalized data including restored standard answers/analysis, and proves score 40 with authoritative per-question teacherScore values 10/10/0/10/10. Rust serializes answer object properties in canonical order; JSON.parse produces the same consumer-visible object. No data path is masked.

The list content is a JSON string with independently generated question UUIDs and serializer property ordering. Parsed/recursively normalized content is identical in the isolated probe; both lists contain exactly one original exam, score 40, and the same authoritative awards. No data path is masked.

The answer entity content is a JSON string with independently generated question UUIDs and serializer property ordering. The isolated probe parses/recursively normalizes it, verifies identical fields/answers, and asserts server-recomputed teacherScore 10/10/0/10/10 and total score 40 rather than client-supplied 999. No data path is masked.

Java defect deliberately not reproduced: saveTheoryKnowledgeExamSelfTesting dereferences absent TestPaperDto while serializing question lists, causing HTTP500 and rollback. Rust rejects before writes with HTTP200/code202/message==description 试卷不能为空, avoiding a system-error response for a correctable request.

Java defect deliberately not reproduced: an empty testPaper {} is accepted and creates a useless empty snapshot and active self-test candidate. Rust rejects the empty object before writes with HTTP200/code202/message==description 试卷不能为空; the frontend always sends a selected full TestPaperDto.

Generated-identity comparison limitation, not behavioural divergence: both responses map the requested floor UUID to the same ordered E/T content (moresKey, moresValue, moresTime and sort match). The two seeded stacks create different floor UUIDs; sweep normalizes UUID values but not object keys. No data path is masked; personal-telegram detail-created/paused/finished also compares the same content as arrays.

Both reject repeated settlement with HTTP200/code208/message 训练已结束. Java TerminalStateException mapper repeats the message in description; Rust retains the shared empty-description envelope. No training or statistics are written.
Both reject raw-content writes after settlement with HTTP200/code208/message 训练已结束. Only description differs (Java repeats the message, Rust empty); content remains unchanged.

Nondeterministic enumeration, not content divergence: Java getSetting uses findAll without ORDER BY, while Rust reads UUID primary-key order. Each stack generates independent UUIDs, so array order cannot match. The frontend parseTelegramBasicSettings groups rows by key and nested type, not position. The isolated settings probe asserts both read responses contain exactly the normalized rows returned by saveSetting; saveSetting itself now preserves and compares input order. No value is masked.

Both reject explicit-null rateDotMinMs with HTTP200/code202/message 训练配置须为非负毫秒值，且上界大于下界; no train is inserted. Java's validation mapper repeats the message in description; the pre-existing Rust create validator sends 点. Planner explicitly deferred description-only parity fixes because frontend reads code/message only. Omitted fields are separately proven to default and succeed.

State artefact, not a Rust defect: TheoryKnowledgeTestService.getByKnowledgeSwfIdAndEnable returns ResponseResult.error("数据异常") when no test exists, exactly like Rust. The probe's Java 200 comes from a test row that Java's own earlier probe write created for swf id 999999 (Rust rejects that write with 202, see RUST_STRICTER).
Rust hardening required by the migration plan (section 4.3): the user entity carries no deviceId, password or token. Java returns deviceId and the SHA-256 token digest in userEntity.
Java answers 208 with description equal to the message; Rust leaves the description empty. The frontend never reads the response-level description.
Java answers 208 through ResponseResult.error(208, message), which leaves description null; Rust sends an empty string. The telex page reads only code and message of a 208.
Same as finish-again: Java's description is null, Rust's is empty.

Java defect deliberately not reproduced. The Vue page creates a training without a duration, and the update path never sets one, so a paused training has duration NULL. Creating the next training of that type makes Java finish the paused one and call Integer.valueOf(duration) in TelexPatTrainStatisticalService.statistical, which throws NumberFormatException: Java answers 202 'Cannot parse null string', rolls the whole save back and leaves the user unable to start a new training until the paused one is finished. Rust counts a missing duration as 0 seconds and succeeds.
Follows from create-next: Java rolled back, so the paused predecessor stays status 2; Rust finished it (status 3).

Java defect deliberately not reproduced (IDOR). EnteringTelexPatService.save finds the record by id and type only, never by owner, and then overwrites the totals and sets createUserId to the caller: any user who knows or guesses another user's record id takes the record over. Rust answers 207 无权限 and leaves the record untouched. The Vue page only ever sends the id it received from findByUserIdAndType for its own record.
Follows from foreign-save: Java handed the record to the other user, so the owner's find returns the empty default; Rust kept it and returns the owner's record.
Follows from foreign-save: Java now shows the taken-over record to the intruder, Rust shows the empty default because nothing was written.

Both stacks refuse (HTTP 200, code 500, nothing written); only the text differs. Java leaks Hibernate's StaleObjectStateException message ('Row was updated or deleted by another transaction ... EnteringTelexPatEntity#<id>') from merging a detached entity with an unknown id; Rust says '训练记录不存在或类型不符'. The page ignores the save response.

Both stacks refuse (code 500, nothing written); Java leaks 'detached entity passed to persist' (an empty id slips past the duplicate check and breaks the persist), Rust reports the missing record. Text-only.

Java defect deliberately not reproduced. findByIdAndType misses (type differs), so Java merges a detached entity that has the existing id and silently re-types the user's record without the one-record-per-type check; it adds/updates the new child-type statistics and leaves the former child-type statistics unchanged. Rust treats an id whose record has another type as 'not found' (code 500, nothing written). The page always sends the type it read the record with.

Follows from the registered retyping defect: Java changed the existing training record from type 6 to 7, so type 6 returns its empty default. Rust refused the retyping and still returns the unchanged type-6 record.
Follows from the registered retyping defect: Java now returns the retyped record for type 7. Rust refused the save without writing and returns the empty type-7 default.

Java defect deliberately not reproduced. A save without a type is not rejected by Java: it persists an orphan record with type NULL (and createUserId set) and a statistics row with child_type NULL. The Vue page always sends the type of the route it was opened with, and the Rust save answers 202 without writing.

Sweep artefact caused by the Java defect above: the preceding empty save left a statistics row with child_type NULL, and EnteringExerciseService.statisticalPage groups by childType (Collectors.groupingBy rejects the null key), so Java answers 500 for that user from then on. Rust never writes such rows and returns the four categories.
